claims.requested_action: Tie E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes
claims.argument: For Pace, the goal is not to increase screen time—it is to make sure technology is available when it provides an educational benefit. Decisions about when and how students use that technology should remain with the educators who know their students and classrooms best.
claims.evidence_quote: For Pace, the goal is not to increase screen time—it is to make sure technology is available when it provides an educational benefit. Decisions about when and how students use that technology should remain with the educators who know their students and classrooms best.

claims.requested_action: Continue considering student poverty and financial resources when determining E-Rate discounts
claims.argument: Reducing the discount percentage would increase the school's share of eligible annual internet cost, competing with other educational needs
claims.evidence_quote: For example, at our current 90% discount, Pace pays approximately $1,386 of our eligible annual internet cost. If our discount were reduced to 80%, our share would double to approximately $2,772. At 70%, our responsibility would increase to approximately $4,158.

claims.argument: Reducing eligible services could disproportionately affect smaller schools and schools with limited local resources
claims.evidence_quote: For Pace, the impact is straightforward: E-Rate currently covers 90% of our eligible recurring internet costs. Losing or significantly reducing that support would immediately create an additional expense for our school and take resources away from students.
